report:
The supplied argument establishes the stated partial transport theorem, including genuine forward ascent for Q₂(√2)/Q₂, singular and nonreduced spaces, ordinary open subspaces, and finite separable quadratic towers. This verdict does not complete original P06.2.

I checked the cited hypotheses and relevant proof bodies in the specified primary versions of [CLD](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2) and [Gubler–Rabinoff](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.13548v2). No manuscript receipt, local artifact, previous verdict, or asserted supporting note was treated as an assumption. The task grants the scope of this audit, but grants none of the mathematical conclusions.

Section 3 reconstructs the finite algebra and topology sufficiently. Bounded coordinate maps identify the completed tensor with A⊕Aa without reducing A. The invariant algebra calculation works in characteristic two. The fibre calculation gives precisely one fixed point or two exchanged points; compactness supplies full-fibre shrinking without assuming a covering. Finite restriction gives a legitimate K-analytic carrier, common unit germs and moment images, and consequently the same ordinary form sheaves. Goodness, strictness, separatedness and boundarylessness survive the required operations. Purity is checked component by component: separability makes the reduced tensor reduced, every upstairs minimal prime contracts to a downstairs minimal prime, and finite integral injections preserve component dimensions. Reduction is used only for this dimension argument.

Sections 4–5 correctly handle the fold. F+σF=1 gives the three-ray relation at every analytic point. The normalization covers vanishing coefficients, nilpotent coefficients, and the region where both normalized magnitudes exceed one. Polarization includes cancellation between opposite differences. The convolution estimates control values, first derivatives and bounded second derivatives. On a cell contained in S=0, both dS and the target tangential derivatives vanish; on a cell with nonconstant S, the remaining second derivative error is confined to a strip of calibrated measure O(ε). Constant cells away from zero cause no persistent error. Refinement can simultaneously respect the fold hyperplanes and the calibration.

The measure estimate is on the supporting skeleton before pushforward, so fibre cancellation cannot conceal total variation. Cauchy–Schwarz applied to the minors of the tangent matrix proves (14). Canonical positive cell densities are finite and retain actual fibre-algebra dimensions and generic lengths. Lower dimensional faces have zero top measure. Singular or conductor contributions on top cells remain included, including top cells lying entirely in folds. The case of moment rank below n has zero top forms.

Section 6 supplies the essential form argument. The tripod one-form vanishes on every compact moment image, which establishes ordinary sheaf nullity. Expanding the identity verifies the signs and factor two in (17)–(18). The orbital forms have affine coefficients, hence zero d′d″. Therefore d′d″Lε=0 exactly, and every Pε is closed for both differentials. These identities remove third and fourth smoothing derivatives before any estimates are taken. Pairing the anti-invariant scalar and differential symbols covers every invariant polynomial superform, including alternating pure-prime and ordered mixed terms. Leibniz expansion then gives the required bounded differentiated families and strip estimates for each fixed polynomial.

Section 7 reaches all compact ordinary (n−1,n−1) tests. The coefficient extension uses the closed-subset hypothesis of CLD 1.9.4. Gaussian convolution followed by Taylor approximation proves coefficient C² approximation on a fixed box; averaging preserves the differential basis factors. This C² argument concerns the original smooth upstairs coefficients, whereas the fold descendants use tangential differentiated convergence. The two-point construction gives exact local descent by gluing invariant units. Fixed downstairs cutoffs give smooth extension by zero and one compact D independent of both approximation parameters. The diagonal choice of εj requires bounds only for each fixed polynomial. Equation (24) follows in total variation, and compact boundedness of h proves (28). No C⁰-density substitute is used.

Section 8 closes both implications. The involution is a K-analytic isomorphism on the restricted carrier. Its calibrated degree is one, while restriction multiplies the calibration by two; cancellation gives legitimate semilinear averaging over E. Scalar projection instead preserves the canonical measure without a degree factor. Thus every approximating pairing equals a downstairs pairing by (30). Downstairs vanishing and differentiated total-variation convergence establish vanishing against every averaged upstairs test, and averaging reaches every upstairs test. The reverse implication follows directly from (30). The ambient checks permit iteration without requiring the composite tower to be Galois.

The Q₂ example is correctly verified: the unequal integral and half-integral valuations prevent cancellation, and every extension unit has |z−σz|≤2^(−3/2)<1. It therefore lies outside the residue-separating-unit condition. No analytic counterexample or negative theorem is asserted. Classical recognition, two-sign regularization, positivity transport and extensions beyond the stated towers remain outside the proved conclusion. No substantive repair or harmless wording correction was needed. Quotations of displayed formulas below are transcribed on one line.

passages.statement: CLD 11.1.1–2: for a complete non-Archimedean field K and a K-affinoid algebra A, M(A) is compact Hausdorff, A is noetherian, every ideal of A is closed, and the natural map M(A)→Spec(A) is surjective.

CLD 11.1.5, 11.1.7 and 11.7.7: rational affinoid neighbourhoods form a neighbourhood basis in an affinoid space and can be chosen inside prescribed ordinary open neighbourhoods; ordinary opens are analytic domains; good analytic spaces have affinoid neighbourhood bases; over a nontrivially valued field every point of a good strict analytic space has a strict affinoid neighbourhood.

CLD 11.1.9 and 11.4.4: affinoid fibre products are represented by completed tensor products; projection from scalar extension by a complete analytic field extension is surjective; a finite algebra over a K-affinoid algebra, equipped with its finite-module Banach topology, is K-affinoid.

CLD 11.2.2–3: analytic separatedness implies topological separatedness; strict affinoid analytic dimension equals Krull dimension; complete scalar extension preserves analytic dimension; analytic domains preserve local analytic dimension; for an affinoid space with minimal-prime components Xi, dimₓX=sup{x∈Xi}dim(Xi).

Gubler–Rabinoff 2.11(3′)–(5′): for an analytic field extension L/K and a morphism Y→Z of K-analytic spaces, ∂(Y_L/Z_L)⊆π⁻¹∂(Y/Z). An ordinary open subspace of a boundaryless analytic space is boundaryless.

passages.statement: Gubler–Rabinoff 2.11(3′)–(5′): for an analytic field extension L/K and a morphism Y→Z of K-analytic spaces, ∂(Y_L/Z_L)⊆π⁻¹∂(Y/Z). An ordinary open subspace of a boundaryless analytic space is boundaryless.

CLD 15.1.1(b), 3.3.3 and 1.9.4: on a topologically separated analytic space, an ordinary (p,q)-form has ordinary open local descriptions as a unit-moment pullback of a coefficient form on a paralinéaire subset containing the moment image. That coefficient form has an ambient Euclidean representative; the extension assertion applies when the paralinéaire subset is closed in the ambient open neighbourhood, which 3.3.3 permits choosing.

CLD 6.2.1–2 and 3.3.12: ordinary smooth forms are G-form sections with tropical descriptions on ordinary neighbourhoods; they form an ordinary sheaf stable under wedge product, J, d′ and d′′. Pullback by the corresponding affine G-tropical morphisms commutes with these operations.

CLD 3.4.1, 3.4.4 and 3.4.6: for a G-tropical chart f:X→V and a coefficient form η on a paralinéaire subset containing f(X), its pullback is zero in the G-form sheaf exactly when η restricts to zero on f(W) for every compact domain W of X. For compact X the corresponding criterion holds in the chart presheaf. In bidegree (0,0), the G-form sheaf embeds into the sheaf of functions.

CLD 15.2.2 and 15.2.9: a good topologically separated analytic space is locally holomorphically separated. On a locally holomorphically separated analytic space, for a closed subset F countable at infinity and an ordinary open cover (Ui) of F, there are locally finite nonnegative ordinary smooth functions χi, each compactly supported in Ui, whose sum equals one near F.

CLD 15.7.1–2: a topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space, equipped with its canonical calibration and analytic boundary, is a tropical space of level n. The tropical structure induced on an analytic domain agrees with the structure obtained from that domain's own analytic structure.

CLD 12.4.1–2 and 5.4.4: a unit-moment image of a compact analytic domain is a compact polyhedral subset with a finite cell decomposition and dimension at most the analytic dimension of the domain. A G-tropical chart on a compact level-n space is pleasant, and its tropical polyhedron is the n-dimensional part of its compact image.

CLD 4.5.1–2, 14.2.2, 14.3.2–5 and 14.5.1–2: the canonical skeletal calibration is standard, strictly positive and G-locally constant. On an adapted cell decomposition, its top-cell volume vectors are constant. The moment-image calibration is its direct image; on a top cell D it is dDτD,∗|e1∧⋯∧en|, where dD is the sum of the finite-flat moment degrees of the skeletal cells above D and τD is the affine inverse of a torus projection injective on D. These degrees use actual fibre-algebra dimensions, including nonreduced lengths.

CLD 5.8.3–5 and 5.10.1(c,d): top-form measures are obtained by calibrated contraction on supporting skeleta. For a pleasant chart f and a Borel coefficient form η of bidegree (p,n), p∈{n−1,n}, the associated Borel measure is locally finite exactly when η restricted to the calibrated tropical polyhedron is locally integrable; then f∗((f∗η)Rad)=⟨η,µΠf⟩Rad. For p=n this also computes the integral. Smooth top forms are finite on compact moment domains, and lower dimensional faces carry zero top measure.

CLD 5.7.2, 7.3.5 and 7.7.5: locally bounded continuous real multipliers are locally integrable against the measures of compact smooth top forms and define integration currents. Differentiation is dual to ordinary form differentiation; in particular the zero-Hessian equation for [h] is tested by the integrals of h(d′d′′α)Rad over all compact ordinary (n−1,n−1)-forms α.

CLD 13.3.1–3: finite moment-fibre degrees are dimensions of the actual finite fibre algebras. Under any complete scalar extension and over any chosen lift of the base point, each local fibre degree is the sum of the local degrees at its lifts, and the total fibre degree is unchanged. The dimension calculation retains Artinian algebra lengths.

CLD 14.3.6 and 15.3.1: for a level-n analytic space, a skeletal subset Σ with canonical calibration µ, and any complete analytic field extension L/K, the canonical calibration of its scalar extension satisfies π∗µL=µ. For every tropically Borel (n,n) G-form ω, π∗ωL,Bor=ωBor; if ω is locally integrable, π∗ωL,Rad=ωRad. There is no extension-degree factor in these scalar-projection identities.

CLD 14.4.3: if F/K is finite and Z is an F-analytic space of level n, its restricted K-analytic structure Z0 has the same dimension and skeletal subsets, and the canonical calibrations on every common skeletal subset satisfy µZ0=[F:K]µZ.

CLD 15.4.1–3: for a morphism f:Y→X between level-n K-analytic spaces that is finite over the complement of a Zariski closed subset of X of dimension less than n, and a locally integrable (p,n) G-form ω with p∈{n−1,n}, f∗ω is locally integrable and f∗((f∗ω)Rad)=dc(f)ωRad, where dc(f) is the calibrated degree.
